Rendering style:
Create an authored editorial illustration for a serious technology newspaper.

Direction:
- authored editorial print language
- deliberate simplified shapes with clear focal hierarchy
- restrained limited palette
- subtle physical print texture
- controlled abstraction and strong negative space
- non-photorealistic but factually grounded representation
- newspaper and social-card readability

Fixed factual and safety restrictions:
- Do not render visible text, captions, headlines, or newspaper typography.
- Do not render logos or trademarks.
- Do not fabricate visible factual evidence.
- Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
- Do not imitate a named or living artist.

Profile-specific exclusions:
- glossy CGI
- luxury product render
- generic futuristic concept art
- cyberpunk or neon
- glowing circuit-board decoration
- floating particles
- heroic centered hardware
- server rack treated as monument or skyscraper
- generic server room
- advertising composition
- airbrushed gradients
- synthetic chrome
- excessive pseudo-technical detail
- malformed or visible text
- labels
- diagrams with words

Exact source facts:
Title: OFFICIAL MICROSOFT AGENT-FRAMEWORK PYPI PACKAGE COMPROMISED
Summary: Versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2 of Microsoft's agent-framework package on PyPI were pushed from the official publisher account and contain a credential stealer that af_runtime_diag.pth launches on every Python startup, even if nothing imports the package. Along with harvesting environment variables, credential files, and other processes' /proc//environ, it requests fresh GitHub Actions OIDC, Azure DevOps OIDC, and Azure managed identity tokens and sends everything to a webhook.site URL. The attacker is believed to still have publishing access, so defenders should treat any install of either version as a full credential compromise and rotate all secrets, CI tokens, and cloud identities that the environment could reach.

Editorial idea:
A trusted software supply chain can become a launch point for credential theft when an official package is compromised.

Central subject:
The compromised Microsoft agent-framework package and the credentials and cloud identities it exposes.

Visual relationship:
An official distribution channel appears trustworthy while silently transferring access to an attacker.

Composition:
Show a sealed parcel moving along a clear production line, with its outer label intact but a concealed opening releasing copies of keys toward an unseen destination; keep the scene literal and restrained, with no branding or readable text.

Permitted literal elements:
A sealed software package represented as a parcel
A production line or conveyor representing the package registry
Credential keys emerging from a concealed opening
A distant receiving slot representing the attacker's collection point

Abstraction level:
medium

Story-specific forbidden elements:
racks
chips
laptops
robots
clouds
shields
arrows
charts
skyscrapers
chess
handshakes
split-screen conflict
logos
rendered text
artist imitation
unsupported physical details

Likely failure modes to avoid:
Depicting the package as visibly malicious from the start
Showing generic hacking imagery without the trusted-channel tension
Suggesting physical theft rather than credential and token exfiltration
Adding unsupported people, locations, or interface details

Global factual restrictions:
Do not fabricate visible factual evidence. Do not imitate a named or living artist. Do not render interfaces or screenshots.
Do not render any words, letters, numbers, labels, captions, annotations, signage, diagrams with text, logos, watermarks, or pseudo-writing anywhere in the image.
If the concept cannot be represented without visible text, represent the relationship through shape, scale, spacing, direction, grouping, interruption, containment, or contrast instead.
